subject: No control of alpha with filled points

messages.author: eca99c51870663ea
messages.subject: No control of alpha with filled points
parts:
Because I like the way they look for plots with points and lines, I've been making some graphs with the filled shapes (21-25). This is a pretty minor bug, but I've found that the fill doesn't seem to follow the specified alpha level, although the outline does. Or maybe it's a feature.

Attached are a scatterplot (generated by the code below) and a zoomed-in view of a PDF with these shapes. In the zoomed-in view, you can see the edge of the white circle underneath the green ring.

df <- data.frame(xval=rnorm(100), yval=rnorm(100))
ggplot(df, aes(x=xval, y=yval)) +
    geom_point(size=5, shape=21, colour="black", fill="white", alpha=.5)

Hi,

I'm not sure I'm following you --- is it the same effect as in the
example attached (the border of the point is partially covering the
interior of the disc). It seems to me that it's a characteristic of the
point symbols to have the line expand symmetrically inside and outside
when increasing the linewidth, and presumably the border is drawn on top
of the interior region at the engine level. But perhaps I misunderstood
your query?

# code

library(ggextra)
qplot(0, 0, geom="blank")+
geom_point2(size=50, shape=21, fill=alpha("grey", 0.5), col=alpha("red",
0.2), lex=20) +
theme_minimal()



Best,

baptiste
